verdictNotes.ship: SHIP: no critical defect; no confirmed regression against live r60; the new-feature majors do not block; the unknown-regression majors are disclosed (a major with an unknown tag does not hold by RUBRIC 3).

shipReasons: No critical defect was found and none is introduced or left reachable: both demo chapters were won and lost-and-retried by real pad and keyboard input, every state read matched, 0 console errors, and the save-data class passed on 12 shipped release fixtures with nothing lost (CHK-024).

PR-0504 (demo wins have no results music, major) and PR-0481 (demo battle start of 12 to 14 s, major) are inside the brand-new demo mode, which does not exist live: by the owner's rule A they are disclosed and do not block.

PR-0478 and PR-0380 (major) carry regressionVsLive unknown: the independent 1600x900 runs on the candidate table show the swap jerks at live levels (Chapter I 4 against 2, Chapter IV 1 against 3) and Mortiorchis jerks only in 2 of 4 runs, so a regression is possible but unproven; a major with an unknown tag does not hold (only a critical does) and both are disclosed. If Bailey sees the Mortiorchis or Bahamut dissolve and dislikes it, the rigs can be left off for the demo.
PR-0379, PR-0459, PR-0148, PR-0099, PR-0295, PR-0461 and PR-0460 (major, carried) are neither introduced by this change nor regressions; they are disclosed and carried into the next batch.

Because this review is of a candidate that is not yet deployed, the exact-artifact comparison and the live verification remain the deploy's and the next review's; this candidate saves data differently (Settings gained titleArtPicked and visualStyle) and CHK-024 passed on it before going public.
disclosed: PR-0478 (major): the two boss rigs' head-size fix is not independently proven and one two-body frame remains at the Bahamut idle-to-attack swap; the two harness trees disagree.
PR-0380 (major): swap jerks of 40 to 48 px on party figures and, in 2 of 4 runs, Mortiorchis dissolving with a 60 to 68 px shift.
PR-0379 (major): every pose change is a see-through dissolve with a double image for 2 to 4 frames.
PR-0459 (major): size continuity across poses is open on Yunalesca and Leblanc (not validly run on the candidate).
PR-0504 (major, new in the demo): demo wins play no results music.
PR-0481 (major): demo battle start takes 12 to 14 s to the first command, with frames up to 1 s (headless GPU; measure on the booth machine).

PR-0148, PR-0099, PR-0295, PR-0461, PR-0460 (major, carried): no owner listening score, stand-in audio in eleven chapters, phone party-prep layout, chapters without a real-key flow, Chapter III greyed Summon rows.

categories.evidence: Combat auditor, round 28 on candidate 660c19bbd. No combat engine or game-data change: git diff 1cea6e937 660c19bbd touches nothing under src/battle, src/data (bar src/data/art/rigTypes.ts), research/ or BattlePresenter*. Full unit suite on the candidate tree with 180 s timeouts: 24,273 passed, 0 failed, 112 skipped (a first 15 s-timeout run under load had 41 timeouts and no assertion failures). Seeded benches with the shipped line: Chapter I 100/100 (seeds 1 to 100, avg 52 turns); other FFX chapters 31 to 40 of 40 (Mirror Aeons 31, Yunalesca 37, Braska 39, Anima 39, Evrae 39, Yojimbo 39, Natus 38, Omnis 38, Via Purifico 40, Sin core 40, Sin face 40); FFX-2 Bahamut 40/40 at Wait and 40/40 at Active; Vegnagun, Leblanc, Fallen Aeons, Den of Woe, Ixion 15/15; Trema 8/15. Wrong lines lose (Chapter I attack-only, defend-only, random 0/90). Demo logs agree with the sources (Seymour Flux 70,000 HP with Mortiorchis 4,000 and the Mortibsorption cycle; Lance of Atrophy then Full-Life; Bahamut Curse / Attack / Impulse / Mega Flare). Held at r27's 9.5: no engine change; deducted for the pad-driven Overdrive windows never being captured (CHK-023) and PR-0460 unchanged and UNVERIFIED.

Encounter data, AI scripts, phases and party builds are byte-identical to live r60. Demo seeds 7, 10 and 12 open with the party menu; the real-input demo win (seed 7, 55 turns) shows the sourced behaviour; Bahamut seed 56 won (42 turns); defeat and retry reach battle in both demo fights. Chapter I wrong lines 0/90. One new minor, PR-0487 (the Auron tip is false at the first menu of six FFX chapters). The auditor proposed 9.4; I hold r27's 8.9 because the reasons for 8.9 are unchanged and not re-tested (Trema about 60 percent and Den of Woe 95 percent at human pace, PR-0227 and PR-0498; hidden chapters that do not punish credible mistakes, PR-0447; and 16 of 19 chapters have no real-key flow on this candidate), and nothing in the candidate changes an encounter. No gain is claimed.

Provisional 8.4 against r27's 8.5, from stills and the continuity strips of the candidate (bundle index-DwMQUoVh.js) at 2560x1440, 2000x1012, 1600x900 and 390x844. Credits: the Echo title is a clean composition; HD-2D reads as a deliberate lit stage and CLASSIC visibly differs; both demo bosses read as large recognisable painted figures with the party whole at booth size; results, pause and phone match their tiles. Debits: PR-0479, PR-0421, PR-0486 re-observed; PR-0507 (rim and shards; the rig lighting is barely perceptible); PR-0478 and PR-0459 still open (CHK-026 UNVERIFIED, the two harnesses disagree); one double-body frame remains at the Bahamut idle-to-attack swap. Static pose census (no browser): 1106 paintings, 829 pass, 79 waived, 0 fail, 198 exempt, 0 rigged (the rigs are outside it). verify-approved on the candidate tree: 917 ok, 0 mismatched, 0 missing.

Build 660c19bbd, candidate, GPU headless Playwright, no black canvas. Candidate-table harness runs alone at 58.7 to 59.8 fps: 0 snaps per minute; Chapter I 4 swap jerks of 40 px or more (worst 47.6) against 2 on live; Chapter IV 1 (47.9) against 3; Mortiorchis jerks of 60 to 68 px in 2 of 4 runs (PR-0380); ghost severity worst 0.365, 0.326 (PR-0379); KO has no fall (PR-0473). The auditor proposed 8.2 and I keep it: the demo flow is responsive (title to first menu in 1.3 to 3.9 s of screen time, but 12 to 14 s to the first command, PR-0481), R3 opens the slab, the reset and attract behave as claimed, and the Escape/B card absorb works. No gain claimed on r27's 8.3 because the one headline motion fix (the 40 ms rig fade) trades one double image for a shorter dissolve that jerks on Mortiorchis in some runs.

Held at r27's 8.7. src/story is unchanged between 1cea6e937 and 660c19bbd (git diff --stat empty), so round 27's reading of the script text stands by that dependency. New this round: the demo skips the story by design, so no new aftermath was read; Chapter IV results are calm as in r27. Carried polish: the Chapter I and II quip, the smiling wedge and Rikku's grin on the sorrowful line (PR-0485). Not re-read this round: the other chapters' scenes.

No number: there is no numeric owner listening score for this mix (docs/audio/OWNER-VERDICT.md; PR-0148, CHK-B1) and agents cannot hear. Nothing is averaged or zeroed.

New polish: PR-0506 (two confirm prompts), PR-0511 (PRESENTATION value), PR-0508 (VISUAL STYLE scope is onboarding). No approved target exists for the picker, QR plate, reset ring or attract reel (PR-0505). Carried and re-observed: PR-0502, PR-0456, PR-0488. No critical or major interface defect found; PR-0295 (phone prep) is carried and was not re-observed.

issues.title: The two boss rigs (Seymour Flux, Bahamut): the head-size fix is applied but not independently proven, and a double-body frame remains at idle-to-attack swaps
issues.game: both (shared rig plumbing; Seymour Flux is FFX Chapter I, Bahamut is FFX-2 Chapter IV)
issues.chapter: seymour-flux, ffx2-bahamut; battle, rig pose swaps
issues.observed: Two harnesses disagree. With the candidate tree's own harness and pose-measure table (114 subjects), three runs alone on an idle host (confirm-cont, confirm-cont2, confirm-cont3, plus the capture owner's cont2) judge the rig swaps by mesh head: Seymour 126 rig swaps, worst 0.5 percent; Bahamut 107 rig swaps, worst 0.6 percent, CHK-026 PASS on both demo chapters (live r60 under the r27 harness: head 8 and 18 percent, FAIL). That measure is the builder's own (the rig mesh head), so it passes by construction (RUBRIC 6a). The independent evidence is the strips, and the Bahamut idle-to-attack strip (confirm-cont3 jerk-000-bahamut.jpg) still shows one frame at -1 with two half-faded bodies and then an 88.8 px head move, as the builder's own strip docs/screenshots/r61-rigs/ch4-idle-to-attack-fade-strip-A-F-B.jpg does. A third run on the review tree's harness with the review tree's older table (78 subjects) read the same rigs as FAIL (Seymour 24.2 percent, Bahamut 39.1 percent); I treat that run as a configuration error (see PR-0512), not as a product reading, but it shows the verdict depends on which table the harness reads.
issues.expected: CHK-026: a figure's head changes by at most 3 percent across a pose swap; CHK-027: a swap reads as one figure (RUBRIC 6a).
issues.repro: node critic/runner/lib/route.mjs seymour-flux win --continuity --pose-measure=D:/pyrefly-release55/docs/target/pose-measure.json against the candidate, seed 1, 1600x900, run alone; same for ffx2-bahamut. Strip: critic/rounds/round-28/confirm/confirm-cont3/ffx2-bahamut-win/continuity/strips/jerk-000-bahamut.jpg
issues.confidence: high that the two harnesses disagree; medium on the residual double-body frame (one strip plus the builder's strip)
issues.requirement: CHK-026, CHK-027, RUBRIC 6a; carried PR-0478 of rounds 26 and 27
issues.fix: Bailey looks at the Bahamut and Seymour idle-to-attack strips and decides for Monday (proposal 1). If the frame is not acceptable: give whole-figure swaps with a large silhouette change a longer or cut-based swap, and keep 40 ms only for near-identical variants.
issues.acceptanceCheck: Idle-to-attack strips show no frame with two bodies both above half opacity; the harness run with the candidate table passes CHK-026 and CHK-027 on both demo chapters and a second, independent head measure (silhouette, not the rig mesh) agrees within 3 percent.

issues.title: Pose swaps still jump: party heads and feet at 40 to 48 px in Chapter I, Rikku's dressphase change in Chapter IV, and Mortiorchis dissolving through a see-through frame with a 60 to 68 px shift in some runs
issues.game: both (Mortiorchis is FFX Chapter I; Rikku is FFX-2 Chapter IV; the rest is shared)
issues.observed: Candidate tree harness with the candidate table, run alone at 58.7 to 59.8 fps: Chapter I, 4 swap jerks of 40 px or more in each of two confirming runs (worst 47.6 and 47.1 px, Kimahri, Tidus; live r60: 2 over, worst 46.9); Chapter IV, 1 swap jerk over the line (47.9 px, Rikku's feet; live: 3). The capture owner's own run (seed 1, a different 244-swap path) additionally counted 8 Mortiorchis feet jerks of 60.4 to 68.2 px at idle, cast and attack swaps, and the gap pass (seed 7, 2560x1440) counted 5 (44.7 to 64.4 px); the strip jerk-000-mortiorchis.jpg shows the creature dissolving through a mostly transparent frame over about 5 frames while the silhouette moves (idle-to-cast is a 312 px feet shift by design). The two confirming runs (352 swaps each, 43 Mortiorchis swaps) had none, so this is path- or timing-dependent: seen in 2 of 4 candidate runs, 0 in the r27 live run. Rikku's costume change is a one-frame hard cut to a different dress, size and stance (fan; jerk-000-rikku). Snaps per minute are 0.
issues.expected: CHK-027: no one-frame jump of 40 px or more at a swap; a swap reads as one figure.
issues.repro: Chapter I seed 1 and seed 7 (demo), real keys, 1600x900 and 2560x1440, candidate harness with its pose-measure table; play to Mortiorchis's first cast (about 28 s) and its Full-Life cycles.
issues.confidence: medium: the measurement is firm in 2 runs, absent in 2; the cause (the 40 ms whole-figure fade of PR-0478, src/engine/rig/RigFade.ts) is suspected, not traced
issues.fix: Hold the fade longer, or register the feet, for rig variants whose centroid moves more than about 100 px between poses; make Rikku's dressphase change a short blend with a held size.
issues.acceptanceCheck: Three consecutive candidate-table runs on Chapter I report 0 Mortiorchis jerks and no jerk of 40 px or more at a swap; Chapter IV at most 1; worst ghost severity under 0.4.

issues.title: Demo (?demo=1) wins play no music on the results screen: the victory cue is started and then stopped by the battle screen's exit
issues.game: both (Chapter I victory-ffx, Chapter IV the quiet pause cue)
issues.chapter: demo Seymour Flux and demo Bahamut, results after a win
issues.observed: The AudioManager snapshot at the results screen reads playing=null, music.current=null, fading empty on both demo wins, although held earlier listed victory-ffx (Seymour) and pause (Bahamut). Two independent runs (the audio auditor and the gap pass at 250 ms for 7 s) agree, and the confirmer reproduced it on the Seymour demo win and traced it: BattleScreenFlow.showResults (about line 522) starts the cue before the swap on the assumption that the post scene has already replaced the battle screen; demo defaults skip the post scene, so the swap runs BattleScreen.exit(), whose audio.stopMusic(0.6) (BattleScreen.ts:1013) kills it. Defeat avoids this because its cue starts after the swap. Non-demo wins show the cue. A booth visitor wins and hears silence.
issues.expected: The results screen of a win loops the chapter's results cue (resultsMusic.ts), in demo mode as everywhere.
issues.repro: ?demo=1, simulated pad, A on Seymour Flux (seed 7) or Bahamut (seed 56), win, read audioDebug when results is up.
issues.confidence: high that the cue is gone (three runs); medium-high on the cause (traced by reading, reproduced once in a browser). Nobody listened.
issues.requirement: CHK-001 / CHK-023: the right cue at each real moment; resultsMusic.ts contract
issues.fix: In showResults, start the victory cue after the swap when the post scene was skipped (opts.skipCutscenes); or have BattleScreen.exit not stop music when results is its successor.
issues.acceptanceCheck: Demo win of each fight: results snapshot shows playing victory-ffx (Chapter I) and pause (Chapter IV) for 5 s; defeat and non-demo wins unchanged; a unit test in tests/unit/results-music.test.ts.
